Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: 
  Description: Quote from chat:
Alistair Doswald: 
I'm starting this topic to have a record of the work necessary/work done on the documentation for the multi-factor PR.
I'm starting work on this now. What I'd like to do is first update the design document to the current state of the design (there's not that much to do), and afterwards maybe split the step-up from the multi-factor into a new design document, as was discussed at one point.
For the user documentation, I've been through it and the following documents need to be updated:
- rest-api: Sections Users (for the new credential methods) and the CredentialRepresentation
- Server admin:
* section 4.5 User credentials, to describe the new management system for credentials 
* section 5.1 Forgot password, due to a change in the flow
* section 6.3 Authentication Flows, this section should describe the new flow logic, and how to use it
* section 6.5.2 Setup and configuration of Keycloak server, due to a change in the flow
* section 6.6.3. Adding X.509 Client Certificate Authentication to a Browser Flow, due to the changes to browser flows
- Server development: section 8 Authentication SPI, subsections 8.1, 8.2 and 8.3, as this has changed quite a bit.
- Authorization services: section 2.2, due to modifications in the credentials tab
- Upgrading: Section 4 Migration Changes, I'm guessing that there will be a section for the migration to keycloak 8.0.0, and there should probably be a section on migrating existing authentication flows. There was some work that was done to automatically migrate authentication flows, but if some people are using custom flows, they may no longer work as expected due to the change in required/alternative execution logic
Marek Posolda: @Alistair Doswald Thanks for the summary regarding docs. I can think of 2 other sections, which may require changes:
- Section 12.10 First Login Flow for Identity brokering: There may be some minor changes needed
- WebAuthn: This is new section in the latest keycloak/keycloak-documentation repository master. It is not yet available in public as it was added after 7.0 release and it's not yet released
We can see if we need to break "Documentation" into more subtasks

High-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Add support for loading SAML SP metadata from URL
  Description: Many SAML IdPs (Gluu, Shibboleth, CAS, WSO2 Identity Server, etc) have the ability to load SP metadata from a URL and automatically update it. This makes ongoing maintenance easier as updating metadata can be difficult because it requires careful coordination between IdPs and SPs.
Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: 
  Description: *Motivation:*
Keycloak does not support automatic update SAML/OIDC IdP metadata. Admin can only import IdP from metadata url. Automatic update will make ongoing maintenance easier.
*Proposal:* 
Implementation is based on Hynek comment for SAML/OIDC IdP in the main issue :
|What would be needed is the following: * Store with the clients in the attributes: What IdP (if any) it comes from; Whether metadata refresh is enabled flag
 * Store with the identity provider: Metadata URL, Last refresh time, Refresh period; Whether to delete clients which are not found in metadata flag; Whether to add clients that are found in the metadata and do not exist
 * Scheduler that would periodically find identity providers that are past refresh time, then find those clients that should be updated and update those
 * Support for SAML and OIDC metadata format|
 admin can select to autoupdate metadata when creating a SAML/OIDC IdP (autoupdate field by default to false). When autoupdate is true, realm admin must fulfill Refresh period field( default 1 day).
For SAML Identity Provider, realm admin must fulfill Metadata URL.
For OIDC Identity Provider, realm admin must fulfill Issuer. Metadata URL automatically become equal to issuer + '/.well-known/openid-configuration'.
Although Realm Admin can update all SAML/OIDC IdP fields, SAML/OIDC IdP fields imported from metadata will be updated during autoupdate. Realm Admin can select/ deselect autoupdate metadata during SAML/OIDC IdP update.
For each automated SAML/OIDC IdP a scheduler that refreshes IdP metadata every refresh period will be created. Every time Keycloak starts, schedulers for autoupdates IdPs will be created.

* enable sharing effective (reuse) of modules of SSO information

* clearly demonstrate the value of docs-as-code and modularization

  Summary: Improvements for camelCase config properties
  Description: Quite a few configuration properties are named using camelCase notation, like e.g.:
{code:none}
theme.staticMaxAge=...
hostname.default.frontendUrl=...
connectionsJpa.XXX.dataSource=...
{code}
This is fine for configuration file and Java properties, but environment variable counterparts (provided OOTB by MP-Config) look ugly:
{code:none}
KEYCLOAK_THEME_STATICMAXAGE=...
KEYCLOAK_HOSTNAME_DEFAULT_FRONTENDURL=...
KEYCLOAK_CONNECTIONSJPA_XXX_DATASOURCE=...
{code}
For the properties like above, we should provide proper conversion of {{camelCase}} to {{UPPER_UNDERSCORE_CASE}}:
{code:none}
KEYCLOAK_THEME_STATIC_MAX_AGE=...
KEYCLOAK_HOSTNAME_DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL=...
KEYCLOAK_CONNECTIONS_JPA_XXX_DATA_SOURCE=...
{code}
Additionally, we could also support alternate {{dash-case}} notation for config files, which seems to be more widely adopted than `camelCase` (by Spring Boot, Thorntail etc.):
{code:none}
theme.static-max-age=...
hostname.default.frontend-url=...
connections-jpa.XXX.data-source=...
{code}

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Optimize front-channel logout - Via IFRAME
  Description: Derived from KEYCLOAK-4899.
{quote}
The algorithm in AuthenticationManager.browserLogout works in a way that:
- It finds the userSession and tracks all the clients supporting backchannel logout. The Logout request is sent to them
- For the frontchannel logout, which is currently supported just for SAML, there is a chain of browser redirects . The particular client redirects back to keycloak after doing it's logout and then Keycloak redirects to other frontchannel client. Keycloak tracks, which client needs to be logged-out through the update on userSession. So currently when there is userSession with N fronchannel clients, there are N+1 updates to the userSession during logout before userSession is finally removed.
\[[~mposolda@redhat.com]\] thinks that for cross-dc, we may optimize to have just 1 write to userSession. We can improve this by:
- Using iframes for the frontchannel logout. There is some discussion on ML [1] . Using iframes has some other advantages and generally it's much better and more robust than browser redirects approach.
[1] 
{quote}
This feature is almost complete and involves fixing a TODO in [this branch| in [this commit|
* 
This would most likely lead to a parameter of client that would define allowed origins to be allowed to load from within IFRAME as set by Content-Security-Policy.
Note that currently the frontchannel logout is only supported by SAML clients.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Optimize LogoutEndpoint.logout() to not enumerate all clients when checking redirect URI
  Description: Currently the LogoutEndpoint.logout() method (the one used for OIDC frontchannel logout) has quite uneffective way for checking redirect_uri. It calls the method RedirectUtils.verifyRealmRedirectUri, which iterates through all the clients and check if sent redirect_uri matches to any of them.
It will be better if we first lookup UserSessionModel and then check that redirect_uri matches to some of the client attached to UserSessionModel. This will be better for:
- performance as we don't need to iterate through all clients in the realm, but just through those attached to UserSession
- security as we will ensure that sent redirect_uri must match to some URL of any authenticated client applications in the current UserSession. Not any random client in the realm.

```
Page has expired
To restart the login process click_here
To continue the login process click_here
```

```
You are already authenticated as different user ... in this session. Please log out first
```

To have a smooth user experience I would like keycloak to have the same behavior.

To be discussed. However, there are two ways of doing that:
- Observe OAuthClients from an Operator and create KeycloakClient CRs on the fly
- Enhance {{OpenshiftClientStorageProvider}} to support this use case as well.
The latter approach has one downside though. It requires the Keycloak instance to reside in the OpenShift cluster to obtain both {{ca.crt}} and an {{access token}} for Kube API. The Operator seems like a bit more flexible approach.
h3. Rough estimate
1-2 weeks for 1 person.
h3. Open questions
The most important question is what kind of architecture fits here. Can we assume that Keycloak will always be deployed in OpenShift? If not than using an Operator supporting external Keycloak would be a way to go.

  Summary: Remove kcinit and text-based authentication flows
  Description: h1. What
kcinit and it's associated text-based authentication flows adds quite a bit of complexity. It was never fully completed and we don't have capacity to complete it.

Remove kcinit and text-based authentication flows and authenticators. Including:
* There's both a Java and a Go kcinit
* Tests - I think they even checkout and build the kcinit go library
* Auth flow stuff, including all the duplicated code/classes for the text mode
* KeycloakInstalled needs to be reverted
There may be other things also affected by kcinit.

  Summary: Default Security Headers provider
  Description: Keycloak currently has a static list of security headers that are added to HTML responses, but does not have any headers on REST responses. It allows customising the headers directly by setting the header values, which is problematic from the point that headers need to be more dynamic.
We should implement a new default security header provider that follows best practices and allows configuration in terms of high-level configuration options rather than by being able to edit headers directly like the legacy provider does.
One important header that we need to harden is the CSP. We should not allow any inline-scripts or inline-css. For the CSP we most likely need some aspects to be configurable on a per-realm basis.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Polish the layout of alerts
  Description: The alerts justs "look weird". I can see at least two or three clear issues with them.
# The message is not centered, it's closer to the bottom of the alert. This is probably caused by the alert title which is present but empty (and therefore not visible) but takes place anyway.
# The alerts are placed in the page "heading box". You can see in the attached screenshot that the box above Personal Info heading is stretched. The alert should probably be placed *above* the "heading box", not inside it.
# We might also want to reconsider how the alerts are displayed. Currently, the alert is placed above the main content pushing it down. But when the alert is closed (either manually or automatically after a few seconds), the main content "jumps up". Let's imagine a user is about to click some button in the main content, moves the mouse cursor, but then then the content together with the button "jumps" because an alert was automatically closed. We should either display the alert as a "floating" box temporarily overlapping the content, or "reserve" a small space for the alerts above the main content which would be empty when no alert is displayed.
# Some animation would be nice when displaying and closing an alert. Currently it looks a bit clumsy.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: WebAuthn: polish after rebase
  Description: After rebase prototype with latest Keycloak master, WebAuthn was added to the prototype as it is already available in latest Keycloak master. We may have some remaining things to discuss & clarify. This JIRA is just to handle this possible remaining work around clarifying those points.
In case we agree that there is nothing more needed, we may just close the JIRA :)
The points were discussed on zulip (room #dev-auth and topic "multi-factor rebase"), so just copy/paste it here:
1) I've added the WebAuthnCredentialModel class (compatible with OTPCredentialModel and PasswordCredentialModel introduced in the prototype) and I've added fields 
"aaguid", "credentialId" and "counter" as part of CredentialData and "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" as part of SecretData. The only reason why I did is, 
that secretData are not displayed in the admin console. See screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-39-46.png
I am not sure if displaying "AttestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" won't make the data too big. But strictly said, WebAuthn credential doesn't have any confidential data. So should be "attestationStatement" and "credentialPublicKey" added to CredentialData too and displayed in the admin console? This will mean secretData will be just empty. WDYT?
2) The WebAuthn works in a bit different way than OTP. The WebAuthn authentication javascript call to "navigator.credentials.get" allows to pass more IDs of webAuthn credentials to the list of "allowed-credentials" and client itself can decide which credential he wants to use. So regarding this, I see few options:
a) The WebAuthnAuthenticator won't inherit from CredentialValidator interface. This means that in the Credentials selector list, which is described here there will be just single label "WebAuthn" . When this label is chosen, the checkbox is displayed when user can select the WebAuthn credentials, which he wants to use. This is the approach, which I used so far and you can see the screenshot how it looks like the screenshot Screenshot-from-2019-10-23-11-15-49.png
b) The WebAuthnAuthenticator will inherit from CredentialValidator interface. So Credentials selector list will contain separate items for each credential with labels like "WebAuthn - yubikey", "WebAuthn - chrome test" . There won't be checkbox selection on the page. So WebAuthn call to "navigator.credentials.get" will be always called just with single allowed credential.
c) Hybrid of 2 options above. There will be 2 labels and when particular label is chosen, the checkbox selection will be displayed as well on the WebAuthn page, but just with the single credential selected by default, which will correspond to the selected label. User has ability to select more credentials if he wants.
3) I removed the attributes from UserModel as I mentioned. Regarding the credentialId, I kept it just as single item in the WebAuthnCredentialData. In the keycloak master, you had it saved defacto 2 times:
a) the user attribute, which corresponds to the Base64URL encoded "rawId" returned from navigator.credentials.create
b) The attribute on the credential, which corresponds to the Base64 encoded of AttestedCredentialData.getCredentialId .
It seems to me from the WebAuthn specification and from my testing with yubikey and chrome testing api, that both those "credentialsId" are defacto same. So is it ok to save it just once in the credential model? In other words, the item returned from "rawId" is not saved.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Unable to add more than 6 acceptable AAGUIDs for WebAuthn
  Description: h2. Summary
Only 6 AAGUIDs can be added to the Acceptable AAGUID field under WebAuthn Policy of the Keycloak Admin Console because the underlying database column only allows 255 characters. We should be able to whitelist more than 6 AAGUIDs. 
h2. Details
An authenticator device used by WebAuthn contains an AAUID that can be used to identify the type of the authenticator. Each AAGUID is 36 characters long including hyphens (ex. 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). 
These AAGUID can be whitelisted in Keycloak Admin Console via Authentication -> WebAuthn Policy -> Acceptable AAGUIDs. This list of AAGUIDs is then converted into one comma separated string by org.keycloak.models.jpa.RealmAdapter.setWebAuthnPolicy() then inserted into the "value" column of "realm_attribute" table in Keycloak's database. 
However, because this column is only 255 characters long, only six AAGUID can be added (6 x 36 AAGUID characters + 5 commas = 221 total characters). Adding more than 6 will fail with an error message. 
There should be support for whitelisting more than 6 AAGUIDs.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: WebAuthn: create authenticator, requiredAction and policy for passwordless
  Description: h3. What
Regarding WebAuthn, we need to ensure that user is able to register WebAuthn Security Key as passwordless authenticator (1st factor) or as 2nd factor authenticator. 
In other words, WebAuthn is example of the credential, which is probably useful as both 1st factor or 2nd factor. There may be different requirement for WebAuthn configuration for those 2 cases. For example for passwordless WebAuthn, it may be needed that "userRequired" is set to "required" in WebAuthn policy and for 2nd factor WebAuthn, it may be needed that "userRequired" is set to "preferred" .
h3. 
h3. How
Proper solution will be the possibility to create "instances" of credential policy rather than rely on java providers. But until that is done, we will go with a workaround, which may be like this:
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnAuthenticator. Something like "WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnRegister. Something like "WebAuthnPasswordlessRegister" . The WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator will be tight to this required action
- Adding another subclass of WebAuthnCredentialProvider like "WebAuthnPasswordlessCredentialProvider" . It will be used by WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator and WebAuthnPasswordlessRegister.
- Adding another tab in admin console. In addition to the current tab "WebAuthn policy", we will add another tab like "WebAuthn PasswordLess Policy" . The existing tab "WebAuthn Policy" may be renamed to something like "WebAuthn 2nd-factor policy" . The admin will be able to configure different policies for passwordless and different for 2nd factor.
- The previous point means that we may need to add some new set of fields to RealmRepresentation object. All the "webAuthn*" properties may have another counterpart for passwordless. For example "webAuthnPolicyRpEntityName" will have "webAuthnPasswordlessPolicyRpEntityName" .
- The WebAuthnPasswordLessAuthenticator, WebAuthnPasswordLessRegister and WebAuthnPasswordlessCredentialProvider will read the configuration from the "passwordless" fields, but otherwise their implementation will be same as for the 2nd factor java classes.
Those points will allow administrator to configure separate policies for 1st-factor and 2nd-factor and add separate authenticators to authentication flow for 1st-factor and 2-nd factor. Also it will allow user to have 2 type of webauthn credentials. Credentials of type "webauthn-passwordless" for 1st factor WebAuthn authentication and "webauthn" for 2nd factor WebAuthn authentication (NOTE: The credential type "webauthn" is already used in latest master, so we will keep it for backwards-compatibility and won't rename it)
This whole thing is a workaround, which will be addressed more properly in the future.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Passwordless WebAuthn Priority
  Description: In a Passwordless WebAuthn deployment, it's typically the preferred option, with password + OTP as a fallback in case the user's browser doesn't support it.
However in Keycloak, manual administrator intervention is required to get the WebAuthn prompt to come first. The priority ordering in the Authentication flow configuration is apparently overridden by the user's own credential ordering, and the standard way of enrolling new users (setting a temporary password) always puts Password first.
Suggestions:
* Enable the authentication flow priority to override the user's credential priority.
* Enable the user to configure their own credential priority along with their password, OTP devices, etc.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: WebAuthn authentication: improve usability by remove checkboxes
  Description: During WebAuthn authentication, we discussed about possible changes like this:
- Don't display the checkboxes of available WebAuthn credentials, which are shown in this slide . Instead of it, automatically try all the WebAuthn credentials of particular user, but just for the particular factor. For example, if WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator is triggered, it will try the WebAuthn passwordless credentials (Credentials of type "webauthn-passwordless"). Otherwise if WebAuthnAuthenticator is triggered, it will try the WebAuthn 2nd factor credentials (Credentials of type "webauthn").
- The attempt to authenticate with WebAuthn (JS call to navigator.credentials.get) will be tried immediately when the page with the WebAuthn authentication is shown. No need for click button "Login" . That's what most other vendors (including Google) do.
- If the attempt of WebAuthn authentication fails, some nice message should be displayed to the user. There will be a possibility to "Try again" and also possibility of "Try another way", but the latter will be displayed just if user has some other alternatives for the 2-factor authentication.
See screenshot google-securityKeyAuthentication.png for an example how Google is displaying the screen for "Try again" or "Try another way"

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Support for attestation statement verification
  Description: First version of W3C Web Authentication support ( KEYCLOAK-9360 ) doesn't have support for attestation statement verification.
This JIRA will require:
- Adding options "Indirect" and "Direct" to Attestation Conveyance Preference in the WebAuthn policy.
- Ensure that proper webauthn4j functions are called based on the requested attestation conveyance preference
- Introducing of apache-kerby-asn1 library as a Wildfly module may be needed for verify android and TPM attestation statements (which will require that RH is able to productize it, so may require some other subtask related to that).
- Ability to obtain trust anchors.
[~tnorimat] mentioned in the design document 
{code}
In order to verify Attestation Statement, keycloak needs to get its trust anchor's certificate. It is plausible to get the trust anchor's certificate in the following ways :
- obtained from FIDO Alliance Metadata Services.
- obtained from an authenticator's vendor.
{code}
Not sure it makes sense, but we can check if we can use the existing TrustStore SPI available in Keycloak. The SPI allows to have set of known trusted certificates. For performance (or other) purpose, it can be beneficial if the certificate of authenticator's vendor is added manually to the truststore file used by Keycloak and hence will be always available without a need to somehow obtain it from the authenticator. That's to be investigated whether this is valid option or not...
When this feature is to be supported, it is needed to consider the above two ways to get the trust anchors' certificates.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Allow user to choose from multiple credential types during registration of 2-factor credential during authentication
  Description: Let's assume we have authentication flow configured like this:
{code}
Auth type   | Requirement
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cookie   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled 
Kerberos   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
Identity Provider Redirector [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled 
Authenticate with Keycloak [x] Alternative [ ] Required [ ] Conditional [ ] Disabled 
 | - Username Password Form [ ] Alternative [x] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - Authenticate with MFA [ ] Alternative [x] Required [ ] Conditional [ ] Disabled 
 | - OTP   [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - WebAuthn  [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
 | - Hardware Token [x] Alternative [ ] Required  [ ] Disabled
{code}
Then let's assume that user doesn't yet have any 2-factor credential (OTP or WebAuthn or Hardware Token) configured on his account. So then he should be required to configure either OTP or WebAuthn credential during authentication. In this case, after he finish password authentication, he should be able to choose if he wants to configure OTP or WebAuthn credential and register one of them. He should be able to go back and select different credential (EG. He first clicks on WebAuthn, but then he change his mind because he doesn't have yubikey and his phone doesn't have bluetooth, so he want to go back and register OTP through the Google Authenticator app on his phone)

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Should not issue tokens if the request doesn't meet the security profile.
  Description: When I created a client policy which have a "client-roles" type condition and a "fapi-1-advanced" profile and created the specified client role at the client's role settings, the following tokens were issued with no error.
- Not sender-constraint. This is because "OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens Enabled" was OFF.
- Signed with RS256. This is because "Access Token Signature Algorithm" and "ID Token Signature Algorithm" were not specified.
- "redirect_uri" is not checked. This is because "Valid Redirect URIs" was "*".
I think it's good that we are not forced to change the client settings to be suitable for each security profile.
This is because one of the client policy's purposes is avoiding the over 40 settings for those security profiles.
It's OK if the client acts suitable for the selected security profile no matter what the client settings are.
But it's NG if the client acts not suitable for the selected security profile (like the above) with no error.

Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Support for default client policies in newly created realms
  Description: h2. what
Makes sure that there is a mechanism, which will allow to have default client policies in newly created realms. This is currently not available for client policies (there are only "global client profiles" but not "global client policies"). It is needed as client registration policies have default registration policies defined in newly created realms. There is a need to either one of the options like:
- Auto-create client policies in newly created realms
- Have global client policies in each realm
- Have pre-defined default client policies in the "default" realm and makes them inherit in newly created child realms. This may depend on "Realm of realms" feature (Realms inheritance), which is not yet available in Keycloak 14
h2. why
This capability may be needed for being able to migrate Client Registration Policies to Client Policies. Because there are currently some auto-created Client Registration Policies in each realm after creation of new realm. There are some other tasks, which may require this feature.

Alistair Doswald: 
I'm starting this topic to have a record of the work necessary/work done on the documentation for the multi-factor PR.
I'm starting work on this now. What I'd like to do is first update the design document to the current state of the design (there's not that much to do), and afterwards maybe split the step-up from the multi-factor into a new design document, as was discussed at one point.
For the user documentation, I've been through it and the following documents need to be updated:
- rest-api: Sections Users (for the new credential methods) and the CredentialRepresentation
- Server admin:
* section 4.5 User credentials, to describe the new management system for credentials 
* section 5.1 Forgot password, due to a change in the flow
* section 6.3 Authentication Flows, this section should describe the new flow logic, and how to use it
* section 6.5.2 Setup and configuration of Keycloak server, due to a change in the flow
* section 6.6.3. Adding X.509 Client Certificate Authentication to a Browser Flow, due to the changes to browser flows
- Server development: section 8 Authentication SPI, subsections 8.1, 8.2 and 8.3, as this has changed quite a bit.
- Authorization services: section 2.2, due to modifications in the credentials tab
- Upgrading: Section 4 Migration Changes, I'm guessing that there will be a section for the migration to keycloak 8.0.0, and there should probably be a section on migrating existing authentication flows. There was some work that was done to automatically migrate authentication flows, but if some people are using custom flows, they may no longer work as expected due to the change in required/alternative execution logic

- Section 12.10 First Login Flow for Identity brokering: There may be some minor changes needed

We can see if we need to break "Documentation" into more subtasks

- Not strictly needed to address the issue above, but optionally, we can improve this executor by add configuration option to check also other client URIs (not just the redirect URI) if they are "https" . Like web origin, root URL and admin URL.

  Summary: Support having large number of realms
  Description: At the moment there are issues with having larger (100+) amount of realms on a single server. We need to investigate and improve this. Known issues are:
 * Queries not optimized for many realms
 * Caches could have issues
 * Master admin "tokens" to big
 * Version upgrade migration takes too long as realms increase
Low-Level Requirement:
  Summary: Enhance Keycloak Web Admin Console Design to Support Scalability
  Description: As current Admin Console design, there will be one client to be created for each other realm other than master during the admin console loading time.
When there is lot's of realms created since last admin console loaded, then there will be lot's of clients to be created in master realm by the API of _/auth/admin/master/console/whoami_, which will take considerable time to load the UI.
Even after the whoami API is loaded, there will be a _/auth/admin/realms
_ request almost after every user interaction in the UI. 
Let's say that when there will be 1K realms in database, these batch data fetch would be not acceptable for the Admin UI data change.
Proposed Design for Web Admin Console
1. Web Admin Console access should just based on the admin user access token, not the 
2. API _/auth/admin/realms
_ should be designed by Pagination base, and this API may also be only trigered once user reach to the page: `auth/admin/master/console/#/realms`, and this web page would also need to support pagination.
3. API _/auth/admin/master/console/whoami_ should be desgined for per request per realm
4. We may not need to create clients like 'xxx-realm' in master realm
